analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. It adds one table row (head line ~1732) in the environment-variable forwarding table, listing DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS with source references to EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (prefillChunkKey, stepTokenBudgetKey). This is documentation only: no code, authorization, attestation, encryption or protocol behavior changes. Supplied evidence is base text lines 1-834 (the changed hunk at head ~1732 is outside the supplied base text) plus the patch excerpt. The base text covers the logout, enroll and cache sections, which are unchanged. The row documents tuning knobs for prefill chunk size and step token budget, which are availability/performance parameters. The relevant threats are T-010 (DoS) and T-029 (resource monopolisation), plus T-041 for cache behavior. Whether the code validates or bounds these environment values, and whether the launchd passthrough forwards them, is not visible in the supplied evidence. An operator-controlled environment variable is within the operator's own trust domain (TB-003), so no consumer-controlled input path is evident. Remaining integration question: if these variables are actually forwarded into launchd and read without bounds, an operator could cause local memory pressure on their own machine. This is not shown by the supplied evidence, so it is not reported as a finding. No threat-model update is needed from this documentation line.
